description: Angle as a base dimension, and its separation from frequency (AMB-066).

cases.rationale: The radian carries dimension `angle`, not dimensionless. This is a deliberate departure from SI, on the same grounds as `count` and `currency` — both already non-SI base dimensions (AMB-066).
Degrees and radians share a dimension, so they remain interconvertible — the separation is from *dimensionless*, not from each other.
Angular frequency. THE case this ruling exists for: with the radian dimensionless this reduced to {time:-1}.

Frequency. Compare .003: the dimension vectors now DIFFER, so rad/s and Hz are incommensurable and no conversion is offered. Under SI's dimensionless radian both were {time:-1}, commensurable, and a factor-of-1 conversion was offered when the truth is omega = 2*pi*f — a 6.28x error passing every dimensional check.
Angle composes normally; only its dimension is new.
An angle divided by an angle IS dimensionless — the exponents cancel like any other base dimension. Separating angle does not make ratios of angles special.
